thread:
incident-bot: Paging: [SEV2] High tail latency detected for streaming endpoints in us-west-2. Alerting rule: streaming.p99 > 3s for >= 5m. Affected service: runtime/stream-proxy. Node group: gpu-pool-3.

sre_maria: saw the alert, jumping in. p99 spiking ~4.2s, p95 ~700ms. Several streaming sessions reported stalls (no progress) around 17:04 UTC.

oncall_jay: oncall here — ack. What's the customer impact?

support_anne: flagged 3 paying customers with active sessions showing partial audio->text hangs. No complete outages, but degraded UX. Customers notified via ticket T-3421.

infra_tom: I'm seeing PCIe/AER/ECC correctable error chatter on node gpu-node-112 in the last 6 minutes from nvml/dmesg. Possible transient ECC spike + thermal ramp.

eng_runtime_lee: adding context: streaming uses long lived KV cache and heavy KV memory. If a GPU enters ECC/thermal mode, KV replay stalls can create backpressure and increase tail latency.

sre_maria: timeline so far: at 17:03 metric drift starts, 17:06 alerts fire. gpu-node-112 shows repeated correctable ECCs and GPU clock governor downshift.

oncall_jay: can we route traffic off that node? Is there an automated fallback?

eng_runtime_lee: yes, runtime supports live spillover. I'm going to enable aggressive fallback routing for streaming route "model-stream-chat-prod" to route->fallback-model-medium. This will reduce throughput but keep latency bounded.

eng_runtime_lee: running command to mark node for no-new-streams:```sh
kubectl label node gpu-node-112 redwood/quarantine=1 --overwrite
kubectl cordon gpu-node-112
kubectl drain gpu-node-112 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=2m
```

infra_tom: note: kernel logs show repeated: "NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: Correctable ECC error detected" and thermal throttle: "GPU 0: Temperature above threshold, reducing clock". Also NVML reports ECC correctable counter climbing.

sre_maria: taking traffic action now: enabling fallback routing + throttling new stream admissions to 1 per second for that route. Will monitor p99.

incident-bot: Runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-ecc-thermal|gpu-ecc-thermal>. Recommended next steps: quarantine node, collect nvml/dmesg logs, notify hardware ops.

infra_tom: collecting logs:```
# nvml summary
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,clocks.sm,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv
GPU 0, A100-SXM4, 89, 98, 1095, 124
```
Temp is high (89C) and correctable ECC spikes present.

sre_maria: p99 down to ~1.1s after fallback enabled. p95 back to ~150ms. Good sign.

oncall_jay: customer-facing note: "We're seeing degraded streaming performance in us-west-2; we've routed traffic to healthy nodes and are continuing mitigation. No data loss expected. ETA for full restoration: 30-60m." @support_anne can you post?

support_anne: Posted to tickets, cc'd account execs and posted status to customers.

eng_runtime_lee: replaying KV caches off gpu-node-112 caused some backlog, so we paused aggressive prefetch to avoid transient overload. Also increased available worker threads on fallback pool.

infra_tom: hardware ops: tagging hardware team and starting node-level tests. Possible causes: flaky DIMM on GPU board, manufacturing ECC noise, or fans not spinning up. Will attempt controlled reboot if metrics don't improve.

sre_maria: collecting traces for a few affected streaming sessions: logs show stall at sequence step ~420 for multiple sessions; backend reports stalled token generation loop spanning ~3.7s. Looks correlated with GPU ECC interrupts.

eng_runtime_lee: extract of runtime logs:```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T17:05:12Z","req_id":"req_9a3","stage":"kv_read","latency_ms":3720,"node":"gpu-node-112","error":"stall detected"}
```
We see asynchronous kernel preemption and retried launches that add tail latency.

sre_maria: mitigation checklist update: quarantine node, reroute traffic (done), notify hardware (done), collect logs (in progress), schedule node reboot if persist.

oncall_jay: any sign of cascading effect to other nodes?

infra_tom: currently isolated to gpu-node-112 and its immediate placement peers. No cluster-wide ECC spike. Telemetry shows other nodes normal.

eng_runtime_lee: initiated temporary scaling of fallback pool + warm-up to absorb traffic. That should reduce risk of another p99 spike.

sre_maria: rolling p99 graph:```
17:01 200ms -> 17:04 900ms -> 17:06 4.2s -> 17:12 1.1s
```

oncall_jay: good. Any decision on reboot now or wait?

infra_tom: I recommend soft-reboot of the GPU driver first (nvidia-persistenced restart + reload kernel module) to avoid VM reboots. If driver restart does not clear ECC counters and thermal persists, then full node reboot.

eng_runtime_lee: command I'm running on node (will do driver restart after draining completes):```sh
ssh root@gpu-node-112 'systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia'
```

incident-bot: Note: Performing driver/module reload may require that no ML workloads are running; draining now ensures safe window.

infra_tom: driver reload executed. Monitoring nvml counters. ECC correctables stopped incrementing post-reload. Temperature slowly falling to 76C.

sre_maria: p99 now stable ~420ms. Streaming stalls not observed in the last 3 minutes.

oncall_jay: great. Do we still want to reboot the node later for hardware validation?

infra_tom: yes we'll run overnight maintenance with hardware team. For now keep node quarantined until full diagnostics. I'll open CH-8940 with hardware ops.

support_anne: updated customers: "Mitigation applied; performance largely restored. We'll follow up with a post-incident note and any RCA. Thanks for patience."

sre_maria: capturing action items: - hardware ops ticket CH-8940 (tom) - postmortem draft (maria) - adjust runbook to include driver-reload step before full reboot (lee) - update alert thresholds to add ECC-correlated filter to reduce noise (jay)

oncall_jay: I'm handing off to next oncall @sre_maria for post-incident work. I'll write handoff note and escalate if customer noise increases.

sre_maria: taking post-incident. I'll own the postmortem and runbook changes. Will include time series plots and kernel logs.

incident-bot: Incident closed to active paging: p99 recovered below threshold for 20m. Create incident channel if needed.

eng_runtime_lee: small follow-up: we'll also add a temporary circuit breaker to streaming route that rejects requests > 60s to prevent resource hogging during partial hardware flakiness.

sre_maria: Thanks team. Final status: mitigated, node quarantined, hardware ticket opened, customers notified. Will post a short postmortem within 48h. :white_check_mark:
